lede: Columbus had last change, so Rick Bowness picked most of these matchups. Columbus played without Conor Garland and Jake Christiansen. Florida played without Sandis Vilmanis and Uvis Balinskis.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Schwindt’s line
notes.text: Rick Bowness sent Lorentz, Williams and Lomberg out for 6:42 of their 8:57 at 5-on-5 against Imama, Schwindt and Hathaway (75%, about 18% with no line matching).

notes.head: Fantilli’s line drew Lundell’s line
notes.text: Voronkov, Fantilli and Nichushkin spent 10:42 of their 16:48 at 5-on-5 against Luostarinen, Lundell and Devine (64%, about 27% with no line matching), and the chances were close, 0.58 to 0.56 expected goals. The only Columbus goal came then.

notes.head: The third line drew B. Tkachuk’s line
notes.text: Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier spent 8:11 of their 13:04 at 5-on-5 against B. Tkachuk, Bennett and M. Tkachuk (63%, about 28% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.43 to 0.24 expected goals.

notes.head: One matchup went wrong
notes.text: Knies, Monahan and Johnson kept drawing Florida’s second line, Verhaeghe, Reinhart and Eller. In those 7:26 Florida had 0.83 expected goals to Columbus’s 0.34. Florida scored one of its four goals then.

foot: Rick Bowness matched about as hard as in his other home games: each line spent 62% of its time against one opposing line, against 33% to 64% in his first nine.
